title: Robustness of the Tier 2 Increments: Repeated Cross-Validation, Specifications, Cohorts, Model Class, and Twin Pairs Held Out

sheets.name: Table S18
rows: Robustness of the Tier 2 Increments: Repeated Cross-Validation, Specifications, Cohorts, Model Class, and Twin Pairs Held Out
Allostatic load with complete twin pairs held out of training

Note. Out-of-fold R² under 5-fold cross-validation, with outcomes residualized on age within fold. Baseline model: Tier 1 for status, or the Wave 1 outcome plus Tier 1 for 9-year change. ΔR² Tier 2 is the full model minus the baseline model; ΔR² Tier 1 beyond the Wave 1 outcome is the baseline model minus the Wave 1 outcome alone. The repeated-CV interval gives the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of ΔR² Tier 2 over 15 repetitions with different fold assignments; it describes stability to the fold partition, not sampling error. Cohort rows fit the change model separately in MIDUS 2 (followed 2004-2009 to 2013-2014) and the MIDUS Refresher (2011-2014 to 2020-2022), each a single cross-validation run in about half the sample. TabPFN R² is from the same 177 predictors and folds. Frailty and cognition models always exclude complete twin pairs; the last rows refit the allostatic-load models with them removed from training, against the primary rows above, and the two cross-sectional rankings shared 17 of their top 20 predictors, with BMI first in both. PhenoAge is the epigenetic benchmark (age-residualized PhenoAge). CV = cross-validation.
